_comment: Preguntas ORIGINALES tipo NIE del capítulo 1.4. No son preguntas reales del examen. Comprueba con tu edición 2027.

questions.scenario: WARD committed a summary-only offence 7 months ago. No special time limit applies to the offence. Can proceedings now be started in the magistrates' court?
options: No, generally proceedings must start within 6 months for a summary offence
Yes, there is no time limit for summary offences
explanations: The CPS cannot override the limit.

questions.scenario: Which offences are subject to the general 6-month time limit under s. 127 MCA 1980?
What is the usual way for a public prosecutor to start proceedings against a person who is not charged at a police station?
options: An arrest warrant in every case
A written charge and a requisition
explanations: That's a disposal, not a prosecution.

questions.scenario: The single justice procedure is mainly for…
options: summary-only, non-imprisonable offences dealt with on the papers

questions.scenario: After charge, the custody officer must release the person unless a ground in which section of PACE applies?
TAYLOR is charged with burglary. He refuses to give his address and the custody officer has no other way of finding it. Which is correct?
options: Detention after charge may be authorised because his address cannot be ascertained
He must be released on unconditional bail
He must be released under investigation
explanations: Not if a s. 38 ground applies.

questions.scenario: Which of the following is NOT a ground under s. 38 PACE for keeping an adult in detention after charge?
options: Reasonable grounds for believing he will fail to appear in court
To prevent him interfering with witnesses
Because the officer in the case wants to interview him again about other offences for convenience
explanations: Correct: convenience is not a ground.

questions.scenario: A 15-year-old is charged and refused bail. Where should he normally be kept until court?
options: Local authority accommodation, unless impracticable (or secure accommodation needed and unavailable)

questions.scenario: Is breach of a court bail condition, by itself, a criminal offence?
options: No – but the person may be arrested and brought before the court

questions.scenario: A defendant on court bail fails, without reasonable cause, to attend court. Which is correct?
options: An offence of failing to surrender under s. 6 Bail Act 1976
explanations: It is more than breach of conditions.

questions.scenario: Under the Bail Act 1976, s. 4, which is correct?
options: Nobody has a right to bail
A person charged with an offence generally has a right to bail, subject to exceptions in Schedule 1
Only juveniles have a right to bail
Bail is only available after conviction

questions.scenario: Which is an example of an exception to the right to bail in Schedule 1 of the Bail Act?
options: Substantial grounds for believing the defendant would commit an offence while on bail
explanations: Victim's view alone is not the test.

questions.scenario: A suspect is released on pre-charge bail. According to the current scheme (⚠ check edition), who can authorise the initial bail period?
Under the post-2022 scheme, what is the initial applicable bail period for pre-charge bail (⚠ check edition)?
Why might pre-charge bail with conditions be preferable to RUI in a domestic abuse case?
options: Conditions such as no contact can protect the victim

questions.scenario: A person on police bail fails to answer bail at the police station. Which power allows arrest without warrant?
questions.manualRef: Blackstone's 2027 · 1.4 · Failure to answer police bail – s. 46A

questions.scenario: Which of these conditions can the police attach to bail after charge (generally)?
options: Not to contact the named victim
A requirement to make a report before sentence
A requirement to attend an interview with a lawyer

questions.scenario: A person is charged. Before being bailed, what is the main purpose of attaching conditions?
options: To secure surrender, prevent offending/interference with witnesses, or for their protection

questions.scenario: A private individual wants to prosecute. How would proceedings usually start?
options: Laying an information to obtain a summons from a magistrate

questions.scenario: Which statement about either-way offences and time limits is correct?
options: They must be prosecuted within 6 months
They must be prosecuted within 12 months
They must be prosecuted within 3 years
There is no general time limit

questions.scenario: A juvenile is charged and the custody officer believes detention is in the juvenile's own interests. Is this a ground under s. 38?
If bail is refused after charge, when must the person be brought before a court?
options: As soon as practicable (normally the next sitting)

questions.scenario: Who decides to extend pre-charge bail beyond the maximum periods that police can authorise?
Which of these is an out-of-court disposal rather than a way to start a prosecution?
explanations: Correct (⚠ framework updated by PCSC Act 2022).

questions.scenario: An offence is committed and an Act creating it says proceedings may be brought within 3 years. Which applies?
options: The specific statutory time limit applies
explanations: s. 127 is subject to other enactments.
